title: Ad-Duha: speak of the blessings
hook: and as for the favor of your Lord, speak of it (93:11)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ad-Duha again, the orphan and the one who asks. Your line was don't turn the asker away. Did someone ask you for something, and did you stay long enough to hear them? Day one hundred eighty-eight.

Think about how people answer the question, how's it going? Most of us have two settings. Complain, because complaining is safe and everyone can join in. Or say fine, and move on, because saying something went well feels like bragging, or like tempting fate. So the good things in a life often go unsaid. The job that worked out, the friend who showed up, the morning the pain was a little less. Ad-Duha, the surah of the morning light, ends on a line that pushes against that habit. After reminding the Prophet of everything he was given, the last word isn't keep quiet. It's the opposite. Today: the last line of Ad-Duha.
screen: `COMPLAIN, OR SAY FINE.` → `THE GOOD THINGS GO UNSAID.` → `THE LAST LINE OF AD-DUHA.`

segments.voice: Surah ninety-three has eleven verses. The last three are a set of three instructions. The orphan: don't be harsh with him. The one who asks: don't drive him away. And then verse eleven, in Pickthall's translation: Therefore of the bounty of thy Lord be thy discourse. The Arabic is short: fa-haddith. Speak of it. Tell it. The same root gives the word hadith, a report, a thing told. So the surah that began with the morning light, and the promise that the later would be better, ends by asking for the good to be told out loud. Commentators read the bounty in more than one way. Some say it means the revelation itself: the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was being told to share the revelation he had been given. Others read it more widely: every favor, from guidance to food to health, is something to acknowledge rather than hide. Many hold both at once. Scholars are careful to separate this from showing off. Speaking of a gift as a gift points past yourself to where it came from. Boasting points back at you. The difference is often just one word: I did this, or this was given to me. A hadith in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi adds a human side: whoever does not thank people has not thanked God. So speaking of the bounty isn't only upward. It's also telling the teacher, the parent, the stranger at the bus stop, that what they gave you landed. The orphan, the asker, the blessing. Three verses, one direction: open hands and an open mouth.
screen: `THREE INSTRUCTIONS TO END THE SURAH.` · `FA-HADDITH — SPEAK OF IT.` · `A GIFT TOLD, NOT A BOAST.` · `THANK PEOPLE TOO.` · then, large: `SPEAK OF THE GIFT.`

segments.voice: Sit, and let two minutes of quiet settle. Bring to mind one good thing from this week, something given, not something you earned. Hold it long enough to see it clearly. Then think of one person you could tell about it, today, in a sentence: this happened, and I'm grateful. If you pray, you can add alhamdulillah. The bell holds the time.
Ad-Duha. The morning light, Surah ninety-three, which closes with speak of the bounty of your Lord. Today's word.
Your line: speak of the gift. Tell one person, today, one good thing that was given to you, and say thank you to someone who had a hand in it. Day one hundred eighty-eight.

howItsDone: Many Muslims make a habit of naming blessings aloud, answering how are you with alhamdulillah and thanking the people through whom good came, while taking care that speaking of a gift doesn't become boasting.

fork.setup: something good happened to you this week. a friend asks how you are. what does the last verse of Ad-Duha point toward?
options: say fine, so it doesn't sound like bragging
tell them the good thing, as a gift
list what went wrong, to be safe
fork.reveal: of the bounty of your Lord, speak. commentators say: tell it as a gift, not as your own achievement.

original.note: Arabic: "then speak of it," from h-d-th, the root of hadith, a report or thing told (Qur'an 93:11).

trapdoor: what you thought: a line about being thankful.
what it means: the favor of your Lord, speak of it: say the good out loud, as a gift, not a boast.
what a scholar hears: haddith shares h-d-th with hadith; some commentators take the bounty as prophethood and the revelation itself, so the verse is also a command to share the revelation.
